content: I wanted to collect some thoughts on this PR: https://github.com/uncch-rdmc/dataverse/pull/99
It builds on top of the work in: https://github.com/IQSS/dataverse/pull/12783

What does this PR do?

It splits the current integration tests into 3 groups that take about the same time to run.

This PR causes 6 GitHub Action runners to run concurrently at the same time, but it pushes down the entire process from PR to test results in about 20-25 minutes flat.

Build Containers ──┬── JSF Tests (chromium) ~ 20 mins
├── JSF Tests (firefox) ~ 23 mins
├── JSF Tests (webkit) ~ 21 mins
└── Integration Tests (Group 1) ~ 18 mins
└── Integration Tests (Group 2) ~ 18 mins
└── Integration Tests (Group 3) ~ 18 mins

So overall this is a very major improvement for development speed.

So, what's the catch? Well, GitHub Free Organizations (like IQSS) have a concurrency limit of 20 runners for the WHOLE org. So this means at max 3 PRs can be processed every 20 minutes for all repos within the org. I linked some numbers onto the PR.
Does "each on its own runner with a fresh Dataverse" mean you're spinning up three instances of Dataverse?
Sounds like a good way to get more work done more quickly! :tada:

If we want to make this experimental PR happen without causing traffic bottlenecks for other developers, we might have to create a separate testing org with a GitHub Teams subscription. That's why I wanted to just start the conversation on how this might look. I don't want to pay GitHub any money.
Do you have a sense of how close we are to maxing out our limits? I'm not even very aware of them. :sweat_smile:

So P99 is essentially worst case, P90 is the average experience. I modeled based on past week's usage, but release times might be more hectic

Right now for P90 we're nowhere near the limits. After 12783 is merged, P90 goes to 53 seconds, and P99 goes to 6 minutes, but this is completely acceptable, since the tests finish 50% faster and the runners get released fast, so overall it is a win no matter what.

With the experimental PR, P90 goes to 3 min and P99 goes to 10 mins. Realistically, this means we would erase any savings that we got with the optimization, and create more overhead. Especially during releases.

Ash Manda said:

Right now for P90 we're nowhere near the limits.

I'm glad to hear this! :sweat_smile:
If I'm able to find a safe way to run the Integration Tests and JSF tests on the same instance in parallel, we would kill two birds with one shot
